the non‐pertubative effects of world‐string instantons and gaugino‐condensation can be included in a way consistent with supersymmetry, the non‐perturabtive corrections to the Kähler potential can be computed and are of the right sign and magnitude to solve the moduli stabilization problem.

(i) the non‐vanishing flux components H3,0 and H2,1 are necessary for moduli stabilization in the weakly coupled theory, (ii) the H2,2 component of the flux can be avoided by using the KKLT mechanism and (iii) the strong coupling problem can be avoided by including the effects of world sheet instantons.

(i) the Hodge structure in type IIB is modified by the inclusion of non‐perturbatively stabilized fluxes and that (ii) the resulting moduli space is not well understood, but (iii) the moduli stabilization can still be achieved in a two‐step procedure.
